exposure: maternal antibiotic treatment (before or during delivery)
outcome: metabolite composition (e.g., indol-3-lactic acid, N-acetyl-tryptophan, indol-3-acetic acid)
cohort: The study included 134 samples from newborns participating in the Central European Longitudinal Studies of Parents and Children: The Next Generation (CELSPAC: TNG) cohort study.
finding: Maternal antibiotic treatment before or during delivery significantly affects metabolite composition and microbial diversity in the stool of both vaginally and caesarean-delivered newborns.
mod_finding: While the mode of delivery impacts microbial development, the positive effect of vaginal delivery on newborns' microbiome is degraded when the mother is treated with antibiotics before or during delivery.
